extracted.intended_audience: individuals and organizations preparing news or press releases for distribution (WebWire users, PR professionals, marketers, communications staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for composing and formatting news and press releases aimed at online readers or targeted media, emphasizing journalistic tone, concise structure, and inclusion of required metadata and contact information for distribution via WebWire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution type and audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguishes 'News Releases' (distribution of properly formatted articles primarily to online news readers to drive website traffic) from 'Press Releases' (distribution targeting media, reporters, registered media outlets and media-only wire services).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the appropriate type based on whether your goal is to engage online readers/searchability or to deliver news to the media for credibility and potential pickup by print/broadcast/online outlets. Use the press release channel when targeting reporters and media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a reporter, not an advertiser (third-person tone)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write as a third person reporter (a neutral, independent voice) rather than using first-person marketing/advertising language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use third-person constructions (e.g., 'According to John Doe, the next version...') and avoid first-person statements ('I, John Doe, was informed...'). Present your message as news, not promotional copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and paragraph count
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases are most effective when they are under 500 words and generally two to three paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be succinct—keep the release short enough that a reader can grasp the message quickly. Ensure the body is more than one paragraph and the final paragraph restates and summarizes key points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline should be creative, one sentence, capitalize the first letter of all words, and not use all upper case letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid exclamation marks (they convey advertising, not news). Make the headline attention-grabbing while maintaining credibility and avoiding gimmicky punctuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: First paragraph essentials (lead)
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with physical location (country, state, city) and date (month, day, year). The first paragraph must capture attention and contain the most relevant information, including the Five W's (who, what, when, where, why) when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize the entire news release in the lead so that if it's the only part read, the reader understands the message. Include a hook to entice further reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body structure and inverted pyramid
rubrics_metrics.description: Body paragraphs should provide progressively more detailed important information, following the inverted pyramid style (most important information and quotes first).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue from the first paragraph with supporting details and quotes from key staff, customers, or subject-matter experts. Ensure correct grammar and clarity to maintain credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Include quotes from key staff, customers or subject matter experts within the body to add perspective and authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure you are cleared to use quotes; verify permissions and accuracy before publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness and angle
rubrics_metrics.description: Have an angle that will appeal to readers and journalists, often by connecting the release to current events or issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame your content around why journalists or readers should care. Provide factual accuracy and sufficient detail to make pickup by media more likely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual accuracy and clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Content may be used by the media; therefore it must be accurate, reasonably detailed, and you must be cleared to use quotes or information about businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm facts, secure permissions for quoted material, and avoid unverifiable or promotional claims that could undermine credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide avenues for additional information (links and resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Internet links and provide avenues for readers to obtain additional information, demos, samples, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All inclusive links must lead to information rather than advertising. Use the provided WebWire submission fields for company/agency name, website, and other online connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information completeness and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Include contact information (name, title, email, telephone, etc.) for the person who can answer questions about the release, and place it within the appropriate online form fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure contact data is accurate and lists someone available to respond to media inquiries (example shown: 'Contact: Jane Doe, Media Relations, janedoe@xyzPR.com, (212) 555-1212').

rubrics_metrics.name: Include legal/administrative details and background
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide trademark acknowledgments, product or event timelines, availability, logistics, background information about persons or organizations, and any applicable disclaimers in paragraph form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed these details within the release body so journalists have necessary context and legal attributions; include background/boilerplate paragraphs about the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final paragraph purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The final paragraph should restate and summarize the key points of your release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the closing to reinforce the main message and ensure readers leave with the essential takeaway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: succinctness and credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain succinct, to-the-point writing and correct grammar to preserve credibility; avoid overtly promotional language and advertising cues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short, clear sentences and accurate presentation increase the likelihood of media pickup. Avoid marketing fluff and grammar mistakes that could reduce trust.
